fix_assessment.rationale: Raw physical-key capture matches the documented design. Remap-aware/nonphysical-key selection is a separate feature contract, not a bug fix that should globally re-enable mappings in capture.

evidence: The example remaps Caps Lock to F24 and cannot select that nonphysical key while shortcut detection suspends mappings.
The linked13280 explanation identifies suspension during capture as intentional.
Current ShortcutControl explicitly enters DetectShortcutWindowActivated before opening detection UI.
judgment.recommended_action: Acknowledge the real configuration gap and route it as an explicit capture-UX feature rather than a remapping engine regression.
judgment.rationale: Do not classify intentional raw-key capture as a generic Keyboard Manager engine failure. The requested capability is an explicit remap-aware/manual nonphysical-key selection mode; it should be designed with recursion, escape and accessibility behavior rather than disabling capture isolation globally.

comment.body: Suspending remaps while detecting a shortcut is intentional so the editor can see physical keys, as discussed in #13280. Your Caps Lock-to-F24 example still exposes a real configuration/accessibility gap: a key that has no physical key needs an explicit selection or remap-aware capture path. That should be scoped as a capture-UX feature with a reliable escape path and clear raw/remapped semantics, rather than turning remapping back on globally during detection. This does not imply the Keyboard Manager remapping engine is failing.

title: Option to disable suspension of keymappings inside module settings.
